tagline: A narrow town strip, with water on either side.
intro: A1A runs south through Beverly Beach and on into Flagler Beach, a thin strip of a town between the Atlantic Ocean and the Intracoastal Waterway. Its six miles of sand take an orange hue from crushed coquina shells, and one fishing pier interrupts them.

The city is named for Henry Flagler, the railroad developer who helped turn East Florida toward the resort trade. A block west of the pier, the town museum keeps everything from colonial plantation artifacts to its World War II encounters with German submarines.

moments.title: Beverly Beach
moments.text: A1A passes through this town of well under half a square mile, 30 miles south of St. Augustine and 23 miles north of Daytona Beach.

moments.title: Flagler Beach Historical Museum
moments.text: Prehistoric bones share the collection with space food and a Flagler Beach city flag that orbited the Earth aboard the Space Shuttle Endeavour.
